title: The throne of grace (Hebrews 4:12–16)
hook: a high priest touched with our weakness: come boldly
tomorrow: can suffering teach anything? Hebrews says even he learned.

segments.voice: Yesterday, tested like us: the Son made like his brethren in all things, and so able to help the tempted. Yesterday's line: able to help.

Some texts get typed and deleted three times: the ones that admit something. The dent in the car. The grade. The thing that got said in anger. Hiding feels safer, for about a day. Hebrews four has a word for the opposite move, and it pictures a throne. A throne usually means distance: guards, a long hall, a careful bow. This one comes with an invitation to walk right up. But first, a line with an edge.
screen: `TYPED, DELETED, TYPED AGAIN.` → `HIDING FEELS SAFER.` → `A THRONE YOU CAN WALK UP TO?`

segments.voice: "For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword." Quick means alive. It reads "the thoughts and intents of the heart." Nothing hides: "all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do." That could sound frightening. Then the writer turns, and names who stands at the center: "Seeing then that we have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession." Hold fast, and then, of all things, come close. "For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin." Infirmities means weaknesses. Not a priest who can't feel what we feel. Then the invitation: "Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need." Look how the two halves fit. The eyes that see everything belong to the one who understands everything. So there's no point polishing the story first. Come boldly: plainly, without hiding, the way a person talks to someone who already knows. And the help is timed: grace to help in time of need. Not before. Not too late. When it's needed.
screen: `SHARPER THAN ANY TWOEDGED SWORD.` · `NAKED AND OPENED.` · `TOUCHED WITH OUR INFIRMITIES.` · `GRACE TO HELP IN TIME OF NEED.` · then, large: `COME BOLDLY.`

segments.voice: Name one need plainly, out loud, in a single sentence, the way you'd say it to a friend who already knows: no polish, no hiding. If you pray, you can bring that sentence straight to the throne of grace; if not, just say it, and let it be heard. One need is enough for today; the rest can wait their turn while you breathe.
The throne of grace. Hebrews four: a high priest touched with our weakness, and an invitation to come near without hiding anything.
Your line: come boldly, for mercy, and grace to help in time of need. That's today.

howItsDone: Some Christians pray Hebrews 4:16 before confession or in hard times, as permission to come to God plainly and without fear.

fork.setup: your little brother broke a favorite mug and hid the pieces. he's scared to say anything. which idea from Hebrews 4 helps most?
options: the one who sees everything also understands: come plainly, without polish.
nothing hides from God, so he'd better be afraid.
wait until there's a perfect explanation, then speak.
fork.reveal: Hebrews pairs eyes that see all things with a high priest touched with our infirmities: so come boldly, for mercy and grace to help.

original.note: Greek: boldness, plain and open speech; behind boldly in Hebrews 4:16.

trapdoor: what you thought: a throne means stay back and bow.
what it means: a high priest touched with our infirmities invites people to come boldly, for mercy and grace in time of need.
what a scholar hears: boldly renders parrhesia, plain, open speech; and the throne is named for grace.

recall: made like us, so able to help

chat.says: scraped dad's truck on the mailbox driving pop home. dad's on shift till 7. i want to hide it.
options: Come boldly: tell him plainly before he finds it. Hiding never makes the scrape smaller.
Wait and see if he notices. Hebrews says God sees it anyway, so why tell?
Write a long apology first so it sounds perfect when he reads it.
chat.meaning: Hebrews pairs eyes that see everything with one touched by our infirmities: so come boldly, plainly, for mercy and help in time of need.
